RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the July 28, 2005/Sravana 6, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal;
Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs; Personnel, Public
Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Science and Technology; Shipping, Road
Transport and Highways; Small Scale Industries; Space; Statistics and
Programme Implementation; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions —20
Doha Summit
*61. SHRI YASHWANT SINHA: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a South Summit meeting
was held at Doha in June, 2005;
(b) whether it is a fact that neither the
Prime Minister nor the Minister of External
Affairs attended this Summit meeting; and
(c) whether as a result thereof India
missed a great opportunity to promote its
case for a permanent seat in the UNSC
with the members of G-77?
Research team to Antarctica
†*62. PROF R. B. S. VARMA:
SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL:
Will the Minister of OCEAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a team of
Indian Scientists is being sent by
Government to Antarctica for research work;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the subject on which the Indian
Scientists would undertake research at
Antarctica; and
(d) by when, the task would be
completed?
Vehicles running on LPG
†*63. DR. A. K. PATEL: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of vehicles running on
authorized L.P.G. in the country, State-wise;
(b) the number of  L.P.G. filling stations
in the country, State-wise, to meet the
requirement of such vehicles;
(c) whether the number of vehicles
authorised to run on LPG is on the high
side in comparison to the available facility
of LPG supply;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(e) the corrective step proposed by his
Ministry in this regard?
Corruption in SAI
*64. SHRI  PRAMOD MAHAJAN:
SHRI R. K. ANAND:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Auditors
of Sports Authority of India have written
to Government alleging corruption in SAI;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken thereon?
Installation of STD/ISD/PCO booths
*65. PROF. M. M. AGARWAL: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of STD/ISD/PCOs
running in the various districts of Uttar
Pradesh at present, district-wise;
(b) the number of such booths proposed
to be  set up in the State during the current
year, district-wise;
(c) the details of amount spent, so far
on the installation of booths in the State;
and
(d) the steps taken by Government in
this regard?
Corruption in administration
†*66. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the general
public of the country has to spend
Rs. 21,068 crores annually in the form of
bribe to solve their general problems;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard;
(c) whether Government have reformed
the administrative functioning to remove
corruption from the administration during
the past years; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Target of Golden Quadrilateral
*67. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the extent of achievement of targets
by end of the year 2005 of first phase
(NHDP) of road development plan—
Golden Quadrilateral, involving four or six
laning of 5,846 KM of National Highways
between Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and
Kolkata;
(b) the percentage of work that remains
to be done and its location; and
(c) the steps Government are
adopting to achieve completion by the target
date?
Indo-China border talks
*68. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether China has expressed its
readiness to solve boundary issue with
India on the basis of equility and
with mutual understanding and
concessions;
(b) whether this was expressed by
Chinese Chief of Army who had

21
discussions with National Security
Advisor, recently in India;
(c) if so, whether both India and China
have now agreed to mutually settle this
issue;
(d) if so, the latest progress in solving
the issue and whether Governments of
India and China have agreed to have
settlement on this border issue; and
(e) by when the final agreement in this
regard is likely to be reached?
Charges for money orders

Will the Minister of COMMUNICA-
TIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the charges for
sending money orders are exorbitantly high;
(b) if so, what steps Government
propose to take to rat

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the July 28, 2005/Sravana 6, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Agro and Rural Industries; Atomic Energy; Coal;
Communications and Information Technology; External Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs; Personnel, Public
Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Science and Technology; Shipping,
Road Transport and Highways; Small Scale Industries; Space; Statistics
and Programme Implementation; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions —155
ISEC and PDDIP Schemes
334. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the details of Interest Subsidy
Eligibility Certificate Scheme (ISECS) and
Product Development Design Intervention
and Packaging Scheme (PDDIPS)
implemented by Government;
(b) the details of funds allocated to States
under these Schemes during the last three
years, State-wise;
(c) whether Government propose to set
up a fund with an initial amount of Rs. 100
crore for the regeneration of traditional
industries; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
 Agro-based industries in NE Region
335. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of AGRO
AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is need
of taking steps to promote agro-based
industries in the rural areas of the country,
more particularly in the North-East Region
ridden with poverty;
(b) if so, the projects and schemes
launched in the North-East region to
provide employment to unemployed
youth; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
 Support to ARIs
336. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that agro and
rural industries in and around metro cities
are nearly extinct due to lack of
Government's support and of upcoming
multinational companies;
(b) the details regarding production of
agro and rural industries in the metro cities
during the last three years;

77
(c) whether any special scheme is
available with Government to boost the
agro industry in the cities; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
 Uranium Mining
337. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Department of Atomic Energy proposed
uranium mining and processing plant at
Nalgonda in A.P.;
(b) if so, the details of the project;
(c) whether the Department has
submitted its proposal before the
Environment Ministry for environmental
clerance; and
(d) if so, the details thereon?
 Affordable sources of energy
338. SHRI MURLI DEORA: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and U.S. are moving
closer on the crucial issue of Civilian
Nuclear energy by giving India access to
Nuclear Energy Technology;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is proposed to set up five
working groups to expedite the matter;
(d) whether first meeting of this Nuclear
Energy Group will be held in the run up to
Prime Minister's U.S. visit in July, 2005;
and
(e) how far U.S. and India ensure clean,
reliable, affordable sources of energy to
keep the economies of both countries
expanding?
 Atomic energy projects under
construction
339. SHRI  LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) what is the generating installed
capacity of atomic energy in our country;
(b) how much atomic energy is being
generated at present against that capacity;
and
(c) whether there are any other such
projects under construction or planning?
 Agreement with Russia
340. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether India is getting any
assistance from Russia to its nuclear energy
programme;
(b) the details of reactor that Russia is
going to supply to India;
(c) whether any agreement has been
signed between India and Russia on this
during recent Presidents visit to Russia;
and
(d) if so, the details thereon?
 Allotment of captive coal mines to
power projects
341. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to allot captive Coal Mines
to power projects;

78
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
number of captive coal mines so far allotted
to power projects;
(c) whether Government are also
considering to introduce coal sector
reforms; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
 Improving the quality of coal
342. SHRIMATI  PREMA  CARIAPPA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that bulk of coal
produced through open cost mining is of
very low quality;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps taken in this regard to
improve the quality of coal by Coal India
Ltd.?
 Upward growth in coal production
